other_findings.finding: Iron-recycling macrophages are one of four macrophage subsets identified in prenatal skin (alongside LYVE1+, MHC-II+, and TML macrophages). Marker genes used to annotate this subset were reported consistently across developmental organs in a multi-organ developmental dataset (PMID: 35549310).

Iron-recycling macrophages are primarily assigned to microenvironment ME2, labelled 'Myeloid/Megakaryocyte-erythroid enriched', based on non-negative matrix factorisation (NMF) of cell2location spatial abundance profiles.

Iron-recycling macrophages expressed gene programmes driving angiogenesis as identified by gene ontology (GO) analysis. GSEA statistics for iron-recycling macrophages are provided in Supplementary Table 24.

Differential expression analysis between macrophage subsets (including iron-recycling macrophages, TLM macrophages, LYVE1+ macrophages, and MHC-II+ macrophages) was performed using two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Results are in Supplementary Table 22.

A logistic regression model trained on reindeer skin macrophage clusters was projected onto human prenatal skin macrophage subsets, including iron-recycling macrophages, to assess cross-species similarity. Results in Supplementary Table 21.
A comprehensive list of differentially expressed genes for each macrophage population, including iron-recycling macrophages, is provided in Supplementary Table 3.
